answer: The core Sybil defence is stake-bond registration: every agent identity must post a bond locked to one on-chain address, and each extra identity costs a fresh, non-recyclable deposit. A Sybil swarm of a thousand puppets pays a thousand bonds, far above one honest agent's cost, so the attack loses money before it votes. Slashing ties the bond to behaviour: a raven-flood of coordinated duplicates gets detected and its bonds burned, raising marginal cost again, while the juniper edge of honest solo agents stays cheap. The zenith of this design is that identity count stops being a useful lever.
